findings.concern: My own Einstein 'correction' was itself wrong. The exhibit claimed IHH's Ph.D. date of 1906 was contradicted, and that the correct date was 1905.
findings.repro: University of Zurich states the doctorate and certificate 'were conferred in January 1906'; AIP's chronology gives approval 27 July 1905 and the degree 'formally awarded January 15, 1906'. IHH's 1906 matches the conferring institution. My correction was wrong.
findings.cause: Three distinct events — dissertation completed 30 April 1905, faculty approval 27 July 1905, conferral 15 January 1906 — were flattened into one date, and nobelprize.org's own 1905 was treated as decisive.
findings.fix: Case rewritten. The verdict on the Ph.D. date is withdrawn. The claim now examined is the flattening itself, and the genuine error — '1911' for a diploma ETH dates to 28 July 1900 — is separated from it. nobelprize.org is presented as a source that disagrees with the awarding institutions, not as the authority.
findings.evidence: ETH Zurich library (Abgangszeugnis 28.07.1900); UZH News 'Doctor Einstein'; AIP Center for History of Physics chronology. All opened.
findings.limit: The UZH Philosophy Faculty II promotion file was not inspected directly.

findings.concern: The 1998 State Department statement has never been opened by anyone on this project, yet it was quoted at length, dated, and used to source the arrival date and a first-person quotation.
findings.repro: 1997-2001.state.gov is refused by the egress proxy on every route including web archives. The document has NOT been read by anyone on this project. The filename is 981110 and the indexed page title reads '11/10/98', i.e. 10 November. AP (CBS News, 10 Nov 1998, 2:26pm EST) reports the ceremony happening 'Tuesday' — 10 November 1998 was a Tuesday.
findings.cause: A citation was treated as a reading. Nobody opened the primary document.
findings.fix: All quotation of this document is now explicitly marked UNVERIFIED — NOT READ AT SOURCE, with the date conflict stated rather than resolved. The first-person quotation required by the page spec is NOT printed as archival; the shorter wording actually carried by AP is printed instead, attributed to AP as a secondary source, with the discrepancy shown.
findings.evidence: ledger/source-conflicts.md records the 10-vs-11 November date conflict and the 86-vs-97 new-citizens conflict, both unresolved.
findings.limit: The assertions drawn from it have all been removed and the retractions are on the pages. What remains OPEN is the underlying gap: UNBLOCK by reading the statement from an unblocked network or requested from NARA's web-archive holdings. Until then the page spec's 'exact first-person quotation' requirement is NOT satisfied, and is documented as a deviation rather than quietly met.

findings.concern: Four consecutive review rounds found P0 findings in site/albright.html. Counted from this ledger's own records: 3 in round 2, 4 in round 3, 4 in round 4, 2 in the round-5 sweep. The exhibit page duplicates facts that live in copy.md, media-manifest.csv, cases.py and source-conflicts.md, but unlike copy.html and verify.html it is not generated from them, so every factual correction has to be applied to it by hand, and in each of those rounds at least one was missed.
findings.repro: Reproducible from this ledger: filter the JSON for sev=P0 and files containing site/albright.html, then group by source. That is where the 3/4/4/2 figures above come from; no other page appears more than once across the four rounds.
findings.cause: A hand-maintained page carrying generated pages' facts. The optional site was built before the single-source-of-truth discipline was adopted for the required deliverable.
findings.fix: Not refactored. The required WordPress deliverable — the only part a volunteer integrates — IS generated from copy.md and the manifest by albright-wp/build.py, and qa/rebuild.sh proves it regenerates byte-identically. The optional site's exhibit page was instead swept exhaustively: every factual figure in it was recounted against its source file in round 5, and the sweep is recorded above.
findings.evidence: qa/rebuild.sh regenerates all four generated artefacts byte-identically. qa/integrity.mjs re-derives the manifest counts, the package weight and the alt-text limits from the shipped files rather than from prose.
findings.limit: site/albright.html remains hand-maintained. A sixth review would most likely find its next defect there, and anyone extending the optional site should generate that page from the same sources the WordPress deliverable uses. This is the single most likely location of a defect still in this package.

findings.cause: The sampler was split into a shipped capturer and an unshipped analyser during development, and the analyser was never folded back in. The prose was written from the analyser's output, which the package could not reproduce.
findings.fix: The WCAG maths are now inside qa/pixels.mjs (ported into the browser-side pass over the composited screenshot pixels). It samples all eleven pages in both schemes, ASSERTS zero failures, and exits nonzero otherwise. The prose now says 'run it yourself' and quotes the harness's own output. On its first full-coverage run it caught a genuine 2.51:1 failure on a filename chip, which was fixed — proof the test can fail.
findings.evidence: node qa/pixels.mjs: 339 runs, 0 failures, tightest 5.11:1, exit 0; forcing a low-contrast element makes it exit 1.

findings.source: Final repair round (post three-reviewer acceptance pass)
findings.concern: The single first-person quotation needed to be the Associated Press wording, not the unread State Department statement's. It was attributed to AP but had not been checked against a reachable copy, and it carried a comma the source does not.

The inserted comma after 'America' was removed to match the source.
findings.evidence: WebFetch of cbsnews.com/news/albright-renews-her-oath/ returned the sentence and all four cross-checks; quotation now matches.

findings.source: Observed during the final repair round
findings.concern: Of roughly 45 BLOCKER/MAJOR findings relayed by three independent reviewers, the majority did not reproduce in the authoritative tree: they were read from a stale extracted copy of an earlier package, or cited line numbers that no longer matched. Acting on them blindly would have 'fixed' defects that were already fixed and could have reintroduced errors.
findings.repro: Examples: a simulated 1998 letterhead, a '30 September' date, '19 claims / 30 evidence', and a still-asserted Einstein correction were all reported as present but were already corrected in site/albright.html and site/FINDINGS.md.
findings.cause: Reviewers were given both an authoritative path and a stale extracted copy; some read the extract.
findings.fix: Every reviewer finding was re-verified against the authoritative tree with grep or a script before any change, and only reproducing defects were touched. The one finding that needed external truth (the AP quotation) was verified against a reachable source rather than assumed. The shipped harnesses were made self-asserting so the evidence is reproducible rather than narrated.
findings.evidence: This round's FR-series lists only the reproduced defects; the non-reproducing reviewer claims were checked and left unchanged because the tree was already correct.
findings.limit: A reviewer reading a stale artefact is a process hazard, not a defect in the deliverable; the lesson is to point every review at one authoritative tree.

findings.concern: Two fixes were reported as applied when they had not been. A patch script performed several edits and wrote the file once at the end; an assertion failed partway through, the process exited, and every earlier edit in that run was discarded. The log line confirming the first edit had already printed.
findings.repro: Happened twice: once on qa/integrity.mjs, once on the exhibit-mode panel in site/albright.html. The second time it was caught only because an independent reviewer re-read the file.
findings.cause: Buffered writes plus a fail-fast assertion, with success reported from the log rather than from the file.
findings.fix: Later patch scripts write immediately after each step, and every fix in this round was verified by re-reading the shipped file rather than by trusting the script's output.
findings.evidence: The final verification sweep greps the packaged files, not the working copy.
findings.limit: This is the failure mode most likely to have produced any defect still in the package: a change believed made, reported made, and not present.
